correctness.rationale: The invariant counts, for each k-vertex unrooted tree T, edge subsets by sorted component-order partition, so the rank k-l(mu) equals the edge-subset cardinality. The source constructs all rooted trees as multisets of child rooted codes and identifies all unrooted trees using their centers; these are exhaustive combinatorial bijections, not sampled graph lists. Independently enumerated every unlabelled tree with NetworkX nonisomorphic_trees(k), k=4..10, and counted all 2^(k-1) spanning forests per tree by connected components, obtaining tree counts 2,3,6,11,23,47,106 and exact tau values 2,2,3,3,4,4,6. At k=10 precisely one pair collides at rank five and none at six; its diameters are 6 and 7. Thus tau(10)=6 while all earlier 4..9 meet floor(k/2). The result is restricted to k<=10, not arbitrary orders or the full CSF tree conjecture.

value.rationale: The least number of retained connected-partition layers that reconstruct every unlabelled tree of a fixed order is a natural sharp inverse-invariant cutoff directly motivated by chromatic-symmetric reconstruction. The first strict departure from a published lower bound and explicit unique obstruction are mathematically informative finite boundary data, not an arbitrary graph example.

limitations: Only finite orders 4..10; no conclusion about all tree sizes or the full chromatic symmetric function conjecture.
